group.description: Semantics, naming, structure, and announcement — whether the surface is legible to assistive technology, as distinct from whether it is legible to the eye (perception) or operable (interaction).

capabilities.title: Every interactive element is named
capabilities.description: Each control exposes an accessible name that describes its action, and an icon-only control never relies on the glyph alone to convey what it does.
capabilities.rationale: Provable today and the single most-exercised capability in the catalog — the overwhelming majority of the 273 authored story expectations are role-plus-name assertions, which is exactly this and nothing more.

capabilities.title: Correct roles and landmarks
capabilities.description: Regions, lists, tables, and forms use the semantic role that matches their function, so assistive technology can offer structural navigation rather than a flat run of text.
capabilities.rationale: The element vocabulary is already WAI-ARIA and the parser validates roles against the ARIA registry, so the contract half is done. What is missing is asserting that a surface declares the landmarks it should have rather than only that declared elements exist.

capabilities.title: Headings form a coherent outline
capabilities.description: Heading levels descend without skipping, and the visual heading size is decoupled from the semantic level so styling never distorts the document outline.
capabilities.rationale: Deterministic from the tree and cheap to check. It becomes load-bearing the moment a Heading primitive separates visual level from semantic level, which is exactly what the target catalog specifies.

capabilities.title: State changes are announced
capabilities.description: Entering a loading, success, error, or offline state produces a polite announcement, so a user who cannot see the change is told about it once and not repeatedly.
capabilities.rationale: Two catalog components (AsyncPanel, VoiceInputButton) already assert announcement behavior through `custom` claims because no typed claim exists for it. This is the capability that would let those be promoted from custom to machine.

capabilities.title: Errors are attached to what they describe
capabilities.description: A validation message is programmatically associated with the control it concerns, and a form-level summary links to the fields it lists.
capabilities.rationale: DESIGN.md requires field-level validation near the affected control plus a form-level summary on submit failure. Association is deterministic from the accessibility tree; whether the message is *useful* is not.

capabilities.title: Status is never color alone
capabilities.description: Every status distinction is carried by text, icon, shape, or position in addition to color, so it survives high-contrast mode and color vision deficiency.
capabilities.rationale: Distinct from perception's forced-colors-legibility, which asks whether the surface remains readable. This asks whether meaning survives when the palette is replaced — the same axis, a different question.

capabilities.title: Perceived order matches programmatic order
capabilities.description: The order content is presented visually matches the order it appears in the accessibility tree, in both reading directions.
capabilities.rationale: The evaluator exists and the claim type is documented as direction-aware, but with no locale axis it has only ever been exercised left-to-right. CSS-reordered layouts are the classic way this breaks and it is invisible without the RTL capture.

capabilities.title: Permission states are explained, not blank
capabilities.description: When a capability is unavailable because permission was refused or not yet granted, the surface explains what is unavailable and what the user can do, without leaking why access is restricted.
capabilities.rationale: `permission-denied` is in the canonical state list and DESIGN.md's state contract, and no scenario has ever captured it. VoiceInputButton is the first catalog asset that genuinely needs the permission axis.
